title: Simple Past: Regular and Irregular Verbs / Nkyerɛaseɛ a εwɔ Awɔdeɛ mu
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, nkyerɛaseɛ a εwɔ awɔdeɛ mu wɔ adansefoɔ a wɔnkyerɛ (hablé, comí, viví). Wɔ English mu, awɔdeɛ a wɔn nyɛ nea wɔde -ed ka ho (talk → talked), nanso awɔdeɛ a wɔn pii wɔ deɛ wɔn nyɛ nea wɔn ho ntɛm (go → went). Enti, wɔ English mu, sɛɛ nea ɛyɛ deɛ ɛyɛ ma wɔn nyinaa (I went, you went, he went), na wɔ Twi mu ɛntɛm (fui, fuiste, fue). Fa akwaba nkyɛn sɛ wopɛ sɛ wode 'did' wɔ kyerɛwom a wɔde ma yɛ akyerɛwoɔ!
rule: Wɔ English mu, nkyerɛaseɛ a εwɔ awɔdeɛ mu de ma awɔdeɛ a wɔn awie wɔ nkyerɛaseɛ biara mu. Sɛ awɔdeɛ no nyɛ nea, εde -ed (work → worked, play → played). Sɛ awɔdeɛ no kɔm wɔ 'e' so, εde -d (live → lived); sɛ ɛkɔm wɔ nhyɛso + 'y', 'y' no ntɛm ma 'i' na εde -ed (study → studied). Awɔdeɛ a wɔn nyɛ nea wɔn ho ntɛm wɔ nkyerɛaseɛ biara mu (see → saw, eat → ate) na ɛsɛ sɛ woka ho nhyerɛn. Wɔ nkyerɛwom a εyɛ nea εyɛ na εyɛ nea εyɛ mu, εde 'did' + awɔdeɛ no nkyerɛaseɛ (I didn't go, Did you see?). Kyerɛwom a εyɛ nea εyɛ no mmom wɔde 'did' ma. Nkyerɛaseɛ a εwɔ awɔdeɛ mu de ma kyerɛwom bɛka 'yesterday', 'last week', 'in 2010'.

title: Present Progressive (Presente Continuo)
bridge: Wɔ Twerefoɔ ne, present continuous (am/is/are + verb -ing) rehwɛ ma wɔde ahyɛ asɛm a ɛrekɔ so anaa a ɛwɔ hyɛn ara nkyɛn. Wɔ Hispanifoɔ ne, yɛde present simple ma yɛbɔ mmara no ho asɛm (''estoy hablando'' vs ''yo hablo''). Nnipa a wɔde Hispanifoɔ kasa no sɛe wɔde verb auxiliary ''to be'' no kɔ so anaa wɔn kyerɛw wɔn ho asɛm ma wɔhu wɔn ho asɛm a wɔde present simple anaa present continuous no ho asɛm. Sɛ yɛbɛka Twerefoɔ ne a, ɛbɛyɛ den sɛ yɛbɛkɔ so (present simple) na ɛbɛyɛ den sɛ yɛbɛkɔ so (present continuous).
rule: Present continuous no de ''to be'' verb no (am, is, are) ne verb a ɛkɔ so no (verb -ing) no. Ɛde ma: 1) asɛm a ɛrekɔ so wɔ kɔkɔ ne (''I am reading now''), 2) asɛm a ɛrekɔ so wɔ hyɛn ara nkyɛn (''She is working in Madrid these days''), na 3) mmara a ɛbɛkɔ so (''We are meeting at 5''). Ɛnde yɛde ma wɔde state verbs (like, want, know, prefer) de, nanso wɔ kyerɛw no ho asɛm. Negative form no de ''not'' a ɛkɔ verb auxiliary no (''I am not sleeping''), na interrogative form no de verb auxiliary no (''Are you listening?''). Wɔ Hispanifoɔ ne, present progressive (estar + gerundio) no yɛ den, nanso Twerefoɔ no de ɛso sɛn biara wɔ Hispanifoɔ no ho asɛm, sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde ma wɔde asɛm a ɛrekɔ so no ho asɛm.

title: Future with going to / Anigyeho ‘going to’
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, sɛ yɛbɛka biribi a yɛbɛyɛ ansa na yɛbɛka ‘ma wɔ akyiri me mɛma me rekɔ sii’. Wɔ English mu, ‘be going to + verb’ yɛ deɛ ɛto ‘ir a + infinitivo’ nti, nanso ɛwɔ hia bi ara: wɔ English mu, ɛsɛ woaka ‘to be’ (am/is/are) anim ‘going to’, na ɛnyɛ adwuma wɔ Twi mu. Enti, ‘going to’ de yɛ ma wɔ apam foforɔ a wɔde bɛka biribi a yɛbɛyɛ ansa na yɛnni adwene so (wɔ nkwa ho wɔde ‘will’ bɛka).
rule: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wɔka ‘going to’ a, woaka: subject + ‘to be’ (am/is/are) + ‘going to’ + verb. Affirmative: ‘I am going to travel’ (Mɛma me rekɔ sii). Negative: ‘I am not going to travel’ (Mennimma me rekɔ sii). Interrogative: ‘Are you going to travel?’ (Wɔbɛma wɔrekɔ sii?). Wɔde ‘I'm going to’, ‘You're going to’ asɛm biara. Wɔde ma: 1) Apam a wɔadwenee (I'm going to study medicine), 2) Adwene a wɔhu (Look at those clouds! It's going to rain). Wɔnni ho nhia ‘will’ (I'll help you). Suhyɛ ‘going to’ mmom a, ‘to be’ na ɛbɛka.

title: Simple Future (will) / Anidaso (will)
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka biribi a ɛbɛba a, yɛnkyɛnkyɛ yɛbɛka 'bɛ-' ama 'bɛba'. Wɔ English, anidaso a wɔkɔ so maa yɛka deɛ ɛbɛba no, ɛne 'will + verb'. Ɛntɛm ne sɛ, ɛnyɛ sɛ Twi, ɛmmfiri ako a onni nhyɛso a ɛde foforo maa obiara. Ntɛm nyɛ sɛ, verb no ɛntɔ nkyɛn wɔ hɔ a, ɛnyɛ sɛ Twi a ɛde foforo maa obiara. Sɛ obi nni ho nhia a, ɛno ne sɛ, obi bɛka 'will' a, ɛno ahyia no verb no ɛde ɛho nhia, na ɛnyɛ sɛ Twi a ɛde '-s' maa obi a ɔwɔ ɛhoɔden no.
rule: Anidaso a wɔde 'will' kyerɛ no, ɛde sɛ, subject + will (anaa ɛnkuro 'll') + verb. Verb no ɛntɔ nkyɛn wɔ hɔ a, ɛnyɛ sɛ Twi a ɛde foforo maa obiara (he will go, she will go, we will go). Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wonee no a, de 'will not' (won't). Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wubɔ hwɛfo a, kyerɛ 'will' maa subject no ahyia no verb no. Wɔde 'will' kyerɛ adwuma a wode ahoɔden bɔɔ no, adwene a ɛbɛba no, nkan ka a wode ahoɔden ka no, na sɛ wopɛ sɛ wokyerɛ sɛ wode ahoɔden bɔ no. Wɔde no kyerɛm nso wɔ nsɛm a ɛbɛba no ho, sɛ tomorrow, next week, soon, etc. Sɛ wonee no a, ɛnkuro no ne 'won't'.

title: Comparatives and Superlatives / Nnyinaso ne Nnyinaso Pa
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, sɛ yɛbɛto nnyinaso ne nnyinaso pa, yɛnkyɛ ‘más’ ne ‘menos’ sɛnea wɔyɛ wɔ Espaniol mu (más alto, el más alto). Wɔ Twimu, ɛnyɛ nsɛmmisa dua: sɛ ɛyɛ nkyerɛasekyerɛase (sɛnea ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ baako anaa mmienu), yɛbɛka ‘-er’ ne ‘-est’ (tall → taller → tallest), na sɛ ɛyɛ nkyerɛasekyerɛase paa (mmienu anaa wɔn ho ban), yɛnkyɛ ‘more’ ne ‘most’ (beautiful → more beautiful → most beautiful). Nokware a ɛwɔ hɔ: mmom nyɛ ‘more tall’ sɛnea wɔbɛka ‘más alto’ — ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ mframa paa wɔ Twimu. Enti, wɔ nnyinaso pa mu, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde ‘the’ ka (the tallest), na wɔ Espaniol mu, ɛnyɛ sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde ‘el’ ka.
rule: Sɛ ɛyɛ nnyinaso a ɛso nnyinaso: Nkyerɛasekyerɛase (sɛnea ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ baako ne mmienu a wɔn mu bi wɔ ‘happy’, ‘simple’) de ‘-er’ (fast → faster). Nkyerɛasekyerɛase paa (mmienu anaa wɔn ho ban) de ‘more’ (more expensive). Sɛ ɛyɛ nnyinaso pa: ‘-est’ (the fastest) anaa ‘most’ (the most expensive). Nkyerɛasekyerɛase mmienu a ɛtwa so wɔ -y de -ier ne -iest (happy → happier → happiest). Mfiti bi a wɔn ho ntɛm: good/well → better → best; bad → worse → worst; far → farther/further → farthest/furthest. Wɔde ‘than’ ka sɛ ɛyɛ nnyinaso (She is taller than me) ne ‘the’ + nnyinaso pa (He is the best). Wɔmmusɛ ‘more’ ne ‘-er’, anaa ‘most’ ne ‘-est’.

Enti, wɔn a wɔtɔ Espaniol kasae wɔn nti, wɔpɛ sɛ wɔbɛka saa ara wɔ Twimu, nanso sɛ ɛyɛ nkyerɛasekyerɛase kɛse a wɔde ‘fast’, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde ‘-er’ ka. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wobɛyɛ ɛha, hwɛ sɛ nkyerɛasekyerɛase no te sɛ ɛyɛ baako (sɛ ɛyɛ saa, de ‘-er’) anaa ɛso mmienu (de ‘more’).

examples.original: The cat is smaller than the dog.
examples.phonetic: /ðə kæt ɪz ˈsmɔlər ðæn ðə dɔg/
examples.translation: Katakyie no te sɛ anoa no.
examples.note: De ‘-er’ sɛ wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛka nnyinaso a ɛwɔ awɛwɛ mu mmienu.

examples.translation: Ɛyɛ abɛntu a ɛte paa wɔ hɔ.
examples.note: De ‘-est’ ne ‘the’ sɛ wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛka nnyinaso pa.

examples.translation: Ɛda a ɛyɛ anɔpa no, ɛyɛ anɔpa pii sɛ ɛda a ɛyɛ.
examples.note: Sɛ nkyerɛasekyerɛase no twa so wɔ asɛm ne din ne asɛm, de asɛm no mmienu (hot → hotter).

levels.label: Long Adjectives: more / most
levels.translation: Nkyerɛasekyerɛase a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ: more / most

examples.original: This exam is more difficult than the last one.
examples.phonetic: /ðɪs ɪgˈzæm ɪz mɔr ˈdɪfəkəlt ðæn ðə læst wʌn/
examples.translation: Nkwagyeɛ yi te sɛ akyi no.
examples.note: Nkyerɛasekyerɛase a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ mmienu anaa wɔn ho ban de ‘more’.

examples.original: She is the most beautiful woman in the room.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi ɪz ðə moʊst ˈbjutəfəl ˈwʊmən ɪn ðə rum/
examples.translation: Ono ne mana a ɛyɛ den paa wɔ hɔ.
examples.note: Nnyinaso pa a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ nkyerɛasekyerɛase a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ mmienu anaa wɔn ho ban de ‘the most’ + nkyerɛasekyerɛase.

examples.original: This phone is more expensive than that one.
examples.phonetic: /ðɪs foʊn ɪz mɔr ɪkˈspɛnsɪv ðæn ðæt wʌn/
examples.note: Afei hwɛ sɛ ‘expensive’ te sɛ ɛyɛ mmienu anaa wɔn ho ban, enti wɔmmusɛ ‘-er’ ka.

examples.original: My dad is a better cook than my mom.
examples.phonetic: /maɪ dæd ɪz ə ˈbɛtər kʊk ðæn maɪ mɑm/
examples.translation: Me papa ne atɔe a ɔte sɛ me mama.
examples.note: ‘Good’ de ‘better’ sɛ ɛyɛ nnyinaso.

examples.original: This is the worst movie I have ever seen.
examples.phonetic: /ðɪs ɪz ðə wɜrst ˈmuvi aɪ hæv ˈɛvər sin/
examples.translation: Ɛyɛ phim a ɛte mmera wɔ hɔ.
examples.note: ‘Bad’ de ‘worse’ ne ‘worst’.

examples.original: She feels happier now than before.
examples.translation: Ono te anaa ɔyɛ anaanasɛm sɛ akyi.
examples.note: Nkyerɛasekyerɛase a ɛtwa so wɔ -y de -ier.

title: Modal Verbs: must, have to, should
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛbɛka 'deber', 'tener que' ne 'debería' maa hyɛ adwuma ne nkwagyeɛ, nanso wɔ English mu, modal verbs fi nkyerɛkyerɛ a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde taa so ara na wɔde nipa ne time. Wɔ hɛn ani, 'must' ne 'have to' yɛ ntɛmponso, nanso wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma, na 'should' de maa hyɛ nkwagyeɛ. Nya daakye: wɔ English mu, modal verbs mmom nte sɛ wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma, na wɔde verb a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma so.
rule: Wɔ English mu, modal verbs de maa hyɛ adwuma (must, have to), nkwagyeɛ (should) ne ho nhia (need to). Maa ka asɛm, yɛbɛka: subject + modal + verb wɔ base form (nte 'to', nte 'have to' ne 'need to' a wɔde 'to'). 'Must' kyerɛ adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma, 'have to' kyerɛ adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma, na 'should' kyerɛ nkwagyeɛ. Wɔ negative: must not (mustn't) maa hyɛ adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma, don't/doesn't have to maa hyɛ adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma, na shouldn't maa hyɛ nkwagyeɛ a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma. Wɔ questions, modal fi nkyerɛkyerɛ a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma ne subject: 'Should I...?' anaa 'Do I have to...?'. Wɔmmɔ 'must' wɔ past; yɛbɛka 'had to'. 'Have to' de wɔ present, past (had to) ne future (will have to). 'Should' yɛ ntɛmponso wɔ past nanso yɛbɛka 'should have + past participle' maa hyɛ nkwagyeɛ a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma, nanso ebi wɔ B1 level.

concept_examples.text: You must wear a seatbelt.
concept_examples.translation: Wɔhwɛ wo sɛ wɔbɛma wo belt.

concept_examples.text: I have to go to work at eight.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛyɛ adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv tuː ɡoʊ tuː wɜːrk æt eɪt/

concept_examples.text: You should drink more water.
concept_examples.translation: Sɛ wɔbɛyɛ adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma, εbɛyɛ sɛ wɔbɛyɛ adwuma.

concept_examples.text: She doesn't have to cook tonight.
concept_examples.translation: Onyame a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma mmom nte sɛ wɔbɛyɛ adwuma.

common_error.wrong: She must to study for the exam.
common_error.correct: She must study for the exam.
common_error.correct_alt: She has to study for the exam.
common_error.explanation: Error a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma: de 'to' a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma 'must'. Wɔ English mu, modal verbs (must, should, can, etc.) de verb a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔmmɔ 'to'. Nanso, 'have to' ne 'need to' de 'to'. Nya daakye: 'must' + verb base, 'have to' + verb base ne 'to'.

examples.translation: Wɔhwɛ wo sɛ wɔbɛma wo bill.
examples.note: Must kyerɛ adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma anaa adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma. Wɔ hɛn ani, ɛte sɛ ɔmanfoɔ a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma.

examples.original: I have to take the bus today.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv tuː teɪk ðə bʌs təˈdeɪ/
examples.note: Have to kyerɛ adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma, sɛ rule anaa circumstance.
Wɔ affirmative, must ne have to yɛ ntɛmponso, nanso must yɛ formal anaa emphatic.

examples.translation: Sɛ wɔbɛyɛ adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma, εbɛyɛ sɛ wɔbɛyɛ adwuma.
examples.note: Should de maa hyɛ nkwagyeɛ anaa recommendation.

examples.translation: Yɛnnyɛ sɛ yɛbɛka sɛ yɛbɛyɛ adwuma today.
examples.note: Negative form yɛ shouldn't, a wɔde maa hyɛ nkwagyeɛ a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma.
Wɔ questions, should de akyire subject.

examples.translation: Wɔmmɔ wo sɛ wɔbɛma wo smoke here.
examples.note: Mustn't kyerɛ adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma. Ɛyɛ strong pɛ wɔ shouldn't.

examples.original: You don't have to arrive early.
examples.translation: Wɔmmɔ wo sɛ wɔbɛma wo arrive early.
examples.note: Don't have to kyerɛ adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde nipa ne adwuma, ɛnte sɛ mustn't. Wɔ hɛn ani, ɛmmɔ wo, nanso ɛnte sɛ ɛyɛ necessary.

examples.original: Do I have to pay now?
examples.translation: Sɛ mɛbɛka sɛ mɛbɛyɛ adwuma now?
examples.note: Maa ka question about obligations with have to, yɛbɛka do/does + subject.

title: Reflexive Verbs / Nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho
bridge: Wɔ Spain nyɛmba no, yɛde nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho pii (me levanto, me baño), nanso wɔ English nyɛmba no, nnkyerɛaseɛ no mmom a wɔde ma wɔn ho nni pii. Pii no, εberɛ a wɔde nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho kyerɛw wɔ Spain nyɛmba no, wɔde kasa kyerɛw wɔ English nyɛmba no (I get up, I shower). Enti, wɔ English nyɛmba no, nnipa a wɔde ma wɔn ho (myself, yourself, etc.) mmom a wɔde no wɔ εberɛ a adwuma no ka ho koraa akyerɛ wo, na nnkyerɛaseɛ no nni nea ɛte saa wɔ Spain nyɛmba no. Fa akwantu sɛ woantwe 'me' kyerɛ 'me' wɔ English nyɛmba no, efisɛ 'me' ne mpanimfo a ɛto so, na ɛnyɛ nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho.
rule: Wɔ English nyɛmba no, wɔde nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho to so (myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves). Wɔde no wɔ εberɛ a obi kɔ so adwuma na ɔnam adwuma no. Nanso wɔ pii no, nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho wɔ Spain nyɛmba no nni nnipa a wɔde ma wɔn ho wɔ English nyɛmba no: get up, wake up, shave, shower, dress, feel, etc. Mfatie: I get up at seven (no 'I get myself up'). I feel happy (no 'I feel myself happy'). Wɔde nnipa a wɔde ma wɔn ho so kyerɛkyerɛ pii: I did it myself. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woto A2, fa akwantu wɔ nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde wɔ adwuma a wɔde wɔ da a ɛda no ho (get up, wash, dress) na nsɛm a ɛte sa 'enjoy oneself' anaa 'behave oneself'. Sonka sɛ 'myself' mmom a wɔde no kyerɛ mpanimfo; wɔ English nyɛmba no, yɛde 'I'.

concept_examples.text: I get up at seven every morning.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛtɔ so wɔ akyaa kɔn a ɛda no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ ɡet ʌp æt ˈsɛvən ˈɛvri ˈmɔːrnɪŋ/

concept_examples.text: She washes her face before breakfast.
concept_examples.translation: Onyin na ɔde ne ho sii animuonyam a ɔbɛyɛ aleɛ.

concept_examples.text: He hurt himself while playing football.
concept_examples.translation: Ɔbaaraa ne ho wɔ atwimfoɔ a ɔredi wɔ.

common_error.wrong: I wash me in the morning.
common_error.correct: I wash myself in the morning.
common_error.correct_alt: I get washed in the morning.
common_error.explanation: Afei akyi, wɔde 'me lavo' wɔ Spain nyɛmba no, na 'me' ne nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho. Nanso wɔ English nyɛmba no, 'me' ne mpanimfo a ɛto so, na ɛnyɛ nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wode nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho kyerɛw, εyɛ sɛ wode 'myself', 'yourself', etc. Nanso pii no, yɛmmusua nnipa a wɔde ma wɔn ho wɔ nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde wɔ adwuma a wɔde wɔ da a ɛda no: 'I wash' anaa 'I have a wash' yɛ kyerɛw a ɛte sɛn. Sonka: wɔ εberɛ a adwuma no ka ho koraa akyerɛ wo, nkyerɛaseɛ pii mmom a wɔde no wɔ English nyɛmba no: I get dressed, I shave, I shower.

levels.label: Daily Routine Reflexive Verbs
levels.translation: Nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho wɔ adwuma a wɔde wɔ da a ɛda no

examples.translation: Mɛtɔ so wɔ akyaa kɔn a ɛda no.
examples.note: Wɔ English nyɛmba no, 'wake up' mmom a wɔde no, na ɛnyɛ nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho, ɛnte sa Spain nyɛmba no.

examples.translation: Onyin na ɔde ne ho sii animuonyam a ɔbɛyɛ aleɛ.
examples.note: Yɛde 'dress' na yɛmfa nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho; 'dress herself' te sɛ ɛyɛ pii anaa ɛnyɛ kyerɛw.

examples.translation: Nnanom na wɔde wɔn ho sii wɔ da a ɛda no.
examples.note: 'Shave' nni nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho wɔ English nyɛmba no.

levels.label: True Reflexive Pronouns
levels.translation: Nnipa a wɔde ma wɔn ho koraa

examples.original: He introduced himself to the class.
examples.translation: Ɔno ara na ɔkɔsii akwantu no so.
examples.note: Yɛn ho nhia 'himself' efisɛ adwuma no ka ho koraa akyerɛ obiara.
Yɛde 'myself' ma yɛkyerɛ sɛ obi ne mpanimfo na ɔne so adwuma.

examples.original: She looked at herself in the mirror.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi lʊkt æt hɜːrˈsɛlf ɪn ðə ˈmɪrər/
examples.translation: Onyin na ɔhwɛe ne ho wɔ apam.
examples.note: Wɔ nkyerɛaseɛ a ɛte sa 'look at' no, nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho yɛ neho.

levels.label: Emphatic and Idiomatic Uses
levels.translation: Nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho na nsɛm a ɛte sa

examples.note: Nkyerɛaseɛ a wɔde ma wɔn ho no kyerɛkyerɛ sɛ obi yɛɛ no ne ho ara.
'Enjoy oneself' ne nsɛm a ɛte sa a ɛkyerɛ 'pasarlo bien'.

examples.translation: Onyin no de ne ho sii pii.
examples.note: 'Behave oneself' ne nsɛm a ɛte sa a ɛte sa wɔ English nyɛmba no.

title: Object Pronouns / Nnwonwa a ɔyɛ de n’asɛm
bridge: Wɔ Twi, nnwonwa a ɔyɛ de n’asɛm (me, te, lo/la, le, nos, os, les) sɛ wo bɛka wɔn ahyia asɛm, na wɔn kyerɛwfo no (me, you, him, her, it, us, them) kɔ so ahyia asɛm anaa ahyia kyɛfa. Enti, wɔ Twi, wɔntɛn sɛde a ɛyɛ de n’asɛm ne sɛde a ɛyɛ de a ɛyɛ n’asɛm no ho asɛm, na wɔn a wɔyɛ de n’asɛm no sɛ wo bɛka wɔn ahyia 'to' anaa 'for'. Fa akwaba: wɔ Twi, ɛnyɛ dɛn na ɛbɛyɛ a wɔbɛtwa nnwonwa no sɛdeɛ wɔyɛ wɔ Castellano no, na ɛnyɛ dɛn na wɔde 'lo' kyerɛ 'it' ma de n’asɛm.
rule: Nnwonwa a ɔyɛ de n’asɛm wɔ Twi no yɛ: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. Wɔde wɔn kyerɛkyerɛ asɛm bi a ɛyɛ de n’asɛm (ɛka asɛm no) anaa ɛyɛ de a ɛyɛ n’asɛm (ɛka de n’asɛm no). Sɛ wo bɛka wɔn ahyia asɛm (I see him) anaa ahyia kyɛfa (She gives it to me) a, ɛno na wɔtɔ wɔn. Wɔn anhwɛ a wɔde wɔn kyerɛ no (him/her ma obi, it ma nnuan, them ma mmara). Ma de a ɛyɛ n’asɛm no, ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde 'asɛm + de n’asɛm + kyɛfa' (She gave the book to him) anaa 'asɛm + kyɛfa + de n’asɛm' (She gave him the book) kyerɛ. Sɛdeɛ ɛyɛ wɔ Castellano no, wɔntɛn nnwonwa bi ma 'le' ne 'lo'; wɔde wɔn kyerɛ him anaa her, na 'ello' de kyerɛ it.

concept_examples.text: I see you every day.
She loves him very much.
Can you give me the book?
We bought them some food.

common_error.wrong: I see her. She is pretty. *I see she.
common_error.correct: I see her. She is pretty.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Castellano no, wɔde nnwonwa a ɛyɛ de n’asɛm (she, he, they) kyerɛ nnwonwa a ɔyɛ de n’asɛm (her, him, them) sɛdeɛ 'la' ne 'le' te sɛ wo bɛka wɔn ahyia asɛm. Wɔ Twi, sɛ wo bɛka asɛm ahyia a, ɛno na wɔde nnwonwa a ɔyɛ de n’asɛm kyerɛ: I see her, ɛnyɛ I see she. Fa akwaba: de n’asɛm = she/he/they; ɔyɛ de n’asɛm = her/him/them.

examples.note: Wɔ Twi, 'him' kɔ so ahyia asɛm, ɛnyɛ sɛdeɛ ɛyɛ wɔ Castellano a wɔde 'lo' kyerɛ no.
Fa akwaba: 'her' de kyerɛ de n’asɛm, ɛnyɛ de a ɛyɛ n’asɛm.
Wɔ Castellano, 'us' de kyerɛ 'nos' na ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde kyerɛ asɛm a ɛyɛ de n’asɛm.
Wɔ Twi, de a ɛyɛ n’asɛm no (me) ɛbɛyɛ a wɔntɛn kyɛfa sɛ ɛkɔ so ahyia de n’asɛm no.
Wɔn a wɔyɛ de n’asɛm no (them) de kyerɛ 'les', nanso wɔ Twi no, wɔntɛn sɛde a ɛyɛ de n’asɛm ne sɛde a ɛyɛ de a ɛyɛ n’asɛm no ho asɛm.

examples.original: Can you buy her a drink?
examples.note: Hwɛ sɛde a wɔde asɛm no: asɛm + nnwonwa a ɛyɛ de n’asɛm + de n’asɛm.

examples.translation: Wɔn frɛɛ me ansa na wɔn.
examples.note: Sɛ wo bɛka kyɛfa 'to' ahyia a, ɛno na wɔde 'me' kyerɛ, ɛnyɛ 'I'.
'you' yɛ de n’asɛm ne de a ɛyɛ n’asɛm, nanso 'me' ne 'us' de kyerɛ sɛde a wɔwɔ kyɛfa mu.
Wɔ Castellano, 'la' kɔ so ahyia asɛm, nanso wɔ Twi, 'her' kɔ so ahyia kyɛfa.

title: Frequency Adverbs / Mmusuo nsɛm a wɔde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm
bridge: Wɔ Twi, mmusuo nsɛm a wɔde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm sɛ 'daadaa' anaa 'ntɛm ara' ntɛm no, wɔde wɔn hyia anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ asɛm no mu ('Daadaa me de me ho adwuma'), nanso wɔ English no, mmara bɔɔ a wɔde no, ɛno na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde wɔn hyia anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ asɛm no mu ('I always do my homework') nanso wɔde wɔn hyia anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ asɛm no mu wɔ 'to be' verb no ho ('I am always happy'). Afei, wɔ Twi no, yɛbɛka 'ntɛm ara' san aa yɛntɔmmorɔ sɛ yɛbɛka 'don't' wɔ English no, na wɔde 'never' maa ɛso ntɛm no.
rule: Mmusuo nsɛm a wɔde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm wɔ English no (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never) no kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no yɛ. Wɔde wɔn hyia: 1) Anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ asɛm no mu: 'She often reads.' 2) Anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ 'to be' verb no (am/is/are) ho: 'He is always late.' 3) Anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ auxilliary verb no ne asɛm no mu wɔ hwɛso ne sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no: 'Do you usually drink coffee?' 'I don't often go out.' Mmra no: 'sometimes' ne 'usually' bɛbu wɔ asɛm no anim anaa akɔso ma ɛto so: 'Sometimes I walk to work' / 'I walk to work sometimes'. 'Never', 'rarely' ne 'seldom' yɛ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no, enti wɔmmusɛ wɔn ne 'not'. Ne 'never' no, de asɛm no ma ɛyɛ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm: 'I never smoke' (nka 'I don't never smoke'). Wɔ hwɛso a ɛso ntɛm no, de wɔn hyia anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ auxilliary verb no: 'Yes, I usually do'.

concept_examples.text: I always have breakfast at seven.
concept_examples.translation: Daadaa me de me ho adwuma wɔ ɛberɛ a ɛfiri anɔpa no.

concept_examples.text: She is often tired after work.
concept_examples.translation: Na ɛno ara na ɛyɛ sɛ wɔde wɔn ho adwuma wɔ ɛberɛ a ɛfiri anɔpa no.

concept_examples.text: They never watch TV at night.
concept_examples.translation: Wɔn a wɔyɛ adwuma no ntɛm ara nhwɛ TV wɔ ɛberɛ a ɛfiri anɔpa no.

concept_examples.text: Do you usually drink coffee?
concept_examples.translation: Sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no, wode no ho adwuma?

common_error.explanation: Ɛbɔ no yɛ sɛ wɔ Twi no, wɔde sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no mmorɔ sɛ wɔde 'ntɛm ara' ma ɛso ntɛm no ('Me nni ntɛm ara nhwɛ TV'). Nanso wɔ English no, 'never' yɛ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no, enti wɔmmusɛ 'don't'. Ma ɛto so, bo mmusuo verb no ho ne de 'never' ma ɛso ntɛm no. Anaa, ɛbɛyɛ sɛ wode 'don't ... ever' nanso ɛnyɛ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no.

levels.label: Position with main verbs
levels.translation: Mmusuo nsɛm a wɔde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no wɔ asɛm no mu

examples.translation: Daadaa me de me ho adwuma.
examples.note: De 'always' hyia anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ asɛm no mu 'brush'.

examples.original: He usually plays football on Sundays.
examples.translation: Ɔno ara na ɔde ɔho adwuma wɔ ɛberɛ a ɛfiri anɔpa no.
examples.note: 'Usually' de hyia anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ asɛm no mu 'plays'.

examples.translation: Wɔn a wɔyɛ adwuma no ntɛm ntɛm no wɔde wɔn ho adwuma wɔ ɛberɛ a ɛfiri anɔpa no.
examples.note: Mmusuo nsɛm 'often' de hyia anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ asɛm no mu 'visit'.

levels.label: Position with the verb 'to be'
levels.translation: Mmusuo nsɛm a wɔde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no wɔ 'to be' verb no ho

examples.translation: Na ɛno ara na ɛyɛ sɛ wɔde wɔn ho adwuma wɔ ɛberɛ a ɛfiri anɔpa no.
examples.note: Anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ 'is' no, yɛde 'always'.

examples.translation: Ntɛm ara me de me ho adwuma.
examples.note: 'Never' de hyia anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ 'am'.

examples.translation: Ɔno ara na ɔyɛ sɛ wɔde ɔho adwuma wɔ ɛberɛ a ɛfiri anɔpa no.
examples.note: Mmusuo nsɛm no de hyia anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ 'is', anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ adjective no.

levels.label: Frequency adverbs in questions and negatives
levels.translation: Mmusuo nsɛm a wɔde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no wɔ hwɛso ne sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no

examples.original: Do you often go to the cinema?
examples.phonetic: /duː juː ˈɒfən ɡəʊ tə ðə ˈsɪnəmə/
examples.translation: Wode no ho adwuma wɔ ɛberɛ a ɛfiri anɔpa no?
examples.note: Wɔ hwɛso no, mmusuo nsɛm no de hyia anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ auxilliary verb no ne asɛm no mu.

examples.original: I don't usually eat fast food.
examples.translation: Me nni sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no de me ho adwuma.
examples.note: Wɔ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no, 'usually' de hyia anim kan deɛ ɛbɛyɛ 'don't' ne asɛm no mu.

examples.translation: Wɔn a wɔyɛ adwuma no ntɛm ntɛm no nhwɛ TV.
examples.note: 'Rarely' yɛ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm no, enti wɔmmusɛ 'don't'.

translations.tw: Mmusuo nsɛm a wɔde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛso ntɛm

title: Prepositions of Time / Nsɛmfa wɔ Nsoromma
bridge: Wɔ Twi, nsɛmfa wɔ nsoromma (at, in, on) wɔ adwuma mma a wɔn a wɔkyerɛ no wɔ Espaniol. Ɛsɛe, yɛse 'on Monday' (Dapaa), 'in the morning' (Wɔ amanɛ), nanso 'at night' (Wɔ adɛnkyɛ). Espaniol de 'en' anaa 'a' wɔ mmerɛ a ɛso nkyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ paa wɔ Twi, na ɛno nti ɛyɛ paa sɛ wɔbɛka wɔn ho asɛm na wɔbɛyɛ nsianka. Bu: wɔ Twi, nsɛmfa biara wɔ hɔ ma wɔde kyerɛ mmerɛ biara: sɛɛ (at), da (on), na mmɛnsa/afom/nsɛnnennen (in).
rule: Wɔ Twi, nsɛmfa wɔ nsoromma a wɔwɔ hɔ ne: 'at' ma wɔde kyerɛ sɛɛ a wɔwɔ hɔ na mmerɛ a wɔwɔ hɔ (at 5 o'clock, at midnight, at noon), 'on' ma wɔde kyerɛ da na nsɛnnennen (on Monday, on July 4th, on my birthday), na 'in' ma wɔde kyerɛ mmerɛ a wɔwɔ hɔ (wɔ 'at night' ho nhia), mmɛnsa, afom, nsɛnnennen na mmerɛ a ɛso (in the morning, in July, in 2024, in summer). Wɔmmusɛ nsɛmfa wɔ 'today', 'yesterday', 'tomorrow', anaa 'this', 'that', 'every', etc. Wɔde 'at' ma wɔde kyerɛ adae a wɔn ho nhia 'day' (at Christmas) nanso 'on Christmas day'.

concept_examples.text: I wake up at seven o'clock.
We have a meeting on Monday.
She goes to the gym in the morning.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃi goʊz tu ðə dʒɪm ɪn ðə ˈmɔrnɪŋ/

concept_examples.text: They travel in summer.

common_error.wrong: I go to work on the morning.
common_error.correct: I go to work in the morning.
common_error.explanation: Nsianka no ara ne sɛ wɔ Espaniol yɛse 'por la mañana' na ɔkyerɛwfo no ka 'por' ne 'on' (ɛfata sɛ 'on' bɛka 'en' wɔ mmerɛ bi). Nanso wɔ Twi, mmerɛ a wɔwɔ hɔ (amanɛ, εbɔnofa) wɔde 'in' ma wɔde kyerɛ no, wɔ 'at night' ho nhia. Ma wɔatwe nsianka no, bu: 'in' ma wɔde kyerɛ mmerɛ a wɔwɔ hɔ, mmom 'on'. Kyɛ kyɛ wɔ nsɛm a ɛte sɛ 'in the afternoon' na 'in the evening'.

examples.phonetic: /ðə klæs stɑrts æt naɪn eɪ ɛm/
examples.translation: Kura no ntɔ so wɔ 9 amanɛ.
examples.note: De 'at' ma wɔde kyerɛ sɛɛ a wɔwɔ hɔ. Wɔ Espaniol wɔde 'a' ma wɔde kyerɛ no, nanso mmom wɔntwe no ho asɛm.

examples.original: She always eats lunch at noon.
examples.note: 'At noon' na 'at midnight' ne mmerɛ a wɔn ho nhia 'in' anaa 'on'.

examples.original: Let's meet at half past five.
examples.note: Wɔde 'at' ma wɔde kyerɛ mmerɛ a ɛte sɛ 'half past' anaa 'quarter to'.

levels.label: On for Days and Dates
levels.translation: On ma wɔde kyerɛ da na nsɛnnennen

examples.note: De 'on' + nsɛnnennen a wɔwɔ da na mmɛnsa. Wɔ Espaniol yɛse 'el 15 de enero', nanso wɔ Twi ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde 'on'.
De 'on' ma wɔde kyerɛ da a wɔwɔ nnɛm, sɛɛ wɔn a wɔwɔ mmiɛnsa anaa wɔn a wɔwɔ mmiɛnsa.

examples.original: We have a party on New Year's Eve.
examples.phonetic: /wi hæv ə ˈpɑrti ɑn nu jɪrz iv/
examples.note: De 'on' wɔ adae a wɔwɔ 'day' anaa 'eve' ho nhia.

levels.label: In for Months, Years, and Seasons
levels.translation: In ma wɔde kyerɛ mmɛnsa, afom na nsɛnnennen

examples.note: De 'in' ma wɔde kyerɛ afom. Wɔ Espaniol wɔde 'en' ma wɔde kyerɛ no, na ɛno nti ɛyɛ paa.
De 'in' ma wɔde kyerɛ mmɛnsa. Mmom 'on' wɔ da a wɔwɔ mmɛnsa no ho nhia.
De 'in' ma wɔde kyerɛ nsɛnnennen, nanso wɔ Twi a wɔatwe no ho asɛm wɔmfa no: 'in winter' anaa 'winter'.

examples.original: The store opens in the afternoon.
examples.translation: Dukan no tɔ so wɔ εbɔnofa.
examples.note: Bu: 'in' ma wɔde kyerɛ 'morning', 'afternoon', 'evening', nanso 'at' ma wɔde kyerɛ 'night'.

title: Conjunctions: and, but, or, because, when, if / Nkɔso: na, nanso, anaa, efisɛ, berɛ, sɛ
bridge: Wɔ Twirifɔtwe, nkɔso no nka sɛnea wɔ Spain wɔ hɔ, nanso yɛnka biara. Sɛnea 'but' no kyerɛw wɔ Twirifɔtwe so, ɛnte sɛ 'pero' wɔ Spain. Wɔ Twirifɔtwe, 'but' no ntumi nka akyi comma wɔ mmrɛso deɛ ɛto so ka ho nsɛm awieε, nanso wɔ Spain, ɛbɛyɛ sɛ wɔde comma no kyerɛw. Enti, 'because' ne 'when' no nni comma wɔ mmrɛso deɛ ɛto so ka ho nsɛm awieε, nanso wɔ Spain, ɛbɛyɛ sɛ wɔde comma no kyerɛw. 'If' no kyerɛw sɛnea 'si' no kyerɛw wɔ Spain, nanso wɔ Twirifɔtwe, subjunctive no nni wɔ A2 level no so.
rule:
Wɔ Twirifɔtwe, nkɔso no de words, phrases anaa sentences ka ho nsɛm awieε. Common nkɔso no ne: 
- 'and' (na) ma ka ho nsɛm awieε.
- 'but' (nanso) ma kyerɛw contrast.
- 'or' (anaa) ma kyerɛw options.
- 'because' (efisɛ) ma kyerɛw reason anaa cause.
- 'when' (berɛ) ma kyerɛw time.
- 'if' (sɛ) ma kyerɛw conditions.

Wɔ compound sentences no, comma no de before nkɔso no wɔ mmrɛso deɛ ɛto so ka ho nsɛm awieε (sɛnea: 'I like tea, but she likes coffee.'). Nanso, wɔ short sentences no, ɛnyɛ nea ɛsɛ. 

Specific rules: 
- 'Because' no de answer 'why' questions. ɛnyɛ nea ɛsɛ wɔ formal writing no, nanso ɛyɛ common wɔ everyday speech no.
- 'When' no de kyerɛw actions deɛ wɔn wɔ specific time; ɛbɛyɛ wɔ beginning anaa middle of sentence.
- 'If' no de kyerɛw condition; wɔ first conditional (sɛ + present, future), 'will' no nni 'if' part no.

Exceptions: 
- 'But' no nni 'although' together, nanso wɔ Spain, 'pero aunque' no yɛ. Wɔ Twirifɔtwe, only one no de.
- 'And' no de lists; before last word no, comma no bɛyɛ optional.
- Wɔ Twirifɔtwe, 'that' no nni nkɔso wɔ these cases no, nanso wɔ Spain, 'que' no yɛ.

concept_examples.text: I like coffee and tea.
She is tired, but she will come.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃi ɪz ˈtaɪərd bʌt ʃi wɪl kʌm/

concept_examples.text: Do you want juice or soda?
We stayed home because it was raining.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː steɪd hoʊm bɪˈkɔːz ɪt wɒz ˈreɪnɪŋ/

common_error.wrong: Because I was sick, so I didn't go to work.
common_error.correct: Because I was sick, I didn't go to work.
common_error.correct_alt: I didn't go to work because I was sick.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Spain, ɛyɛ common sɛ wɔde 'porque' ne 'así que' ka ho nsɛm awieε, nanso wɔ Twirifɔtwe, 'because' no kyerɛw cause no enti 'so' (así que) no nni. To avoid this error, choose only one conjunction: if you use 'because', main sentence no de after; if you use 'so', cause no de first part. Sɛnea: 'I was sick, so I didn't go to work.'

examples.original: I have a cat and a dog.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə kæt ænd ə dɒg/
examples.note: Use 'and' to join two similar elements, just like 'y' in Spanish.

examples.original: He is young but very smart.
examples.note: Use 'but' to contrast, like 'pero'. Don't forget that in English, no comma is used here because it's a short sentence.

examples.original: You can have tea or coffee.
examples.translation: You can take tea anaa coffee.
examples.note: Use 'or' to offer options, equivalent to 'o' in Spanish.

examples.original: She cries because she is happy.
examples.note: Use 'because' to give the reason. In English, no comma is used when the reason clause comes after the main clause.
Use 'when' for time. In English, present simple is used after 'when' for future (not 'llamarás'), unlike in Spanish.

examples.original: When it rains, we stay at home.
examples.phonetic: /wen ɪt reɪnz wiː steɪ æt hoʊm/
examples.note: When 'when' is at the beginning, it's separated by a comma. Note that present tense is used in English, just like in Spanish (not 'lloverá').

examples.original: If you are tired, go to bed.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf juː ɑːr ˈtaɪərd ɡoʊ tuː bed/
examples.translation: Sɛ you tired, go to bed.
examples.note: Use 'if' for real conditions. The clause with 'if' can be at the beginning (with a comma) or at the end (without a comma).

examples.original: I will come if you invite me.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɪl kʌm ɪf juː ɪnˈvaɪt miː/
examples.note: In the first conditional, the part with 'if' doesn't have 'will' (not 'if you will invite').

examples.original: If you study, you will pass.
examples.translation: Sɛ you study, you will pass.
examples.note: Remember that in English, present simple is used in the condition, and future in the consequence. In Spanish, sometimes future is used in both, but in English, it's not.

title: Present Perfect Basics / Mmusuo a ɛyɛ Adwene
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnka pretérito perfecto compuesto (he comido) ma ahyɛseɛ a ɛda bɛyɛ a, na ɛwɔ hɔ ara na ɛyɛ adwene. Wɔ English, present perfect (I have eaten) nea ɛyɛ so, nanso ɛnsɛ so ara na ɛde hyɛnsa a ɛnyɛ adwene biara, na ɛno wɔ Twi a wɔde pretérito indefinido (comí) ka. Mmusuo bi nso ka: wɔ English, present perfect mmom nni adwene a wɔde 'yesterday' anaa 'last year' ka; wɔ nhwɛso no mu, wɔde past simple. Fa akoma hyɛ 'already', 'just' na 'yet' asɛm, efisɛ ɛnsɛ so ara na ɛyɛ wɔ Twi.
rule: Present perfect de bɔɔ so wɔ HAVE (have/has) + participio pasado a ɛyɛ verb no. Verbos a wɔn ni regular no, participio no nea ɛyɛ past simple no (ɛkyerɛ -ed: work -> worked). Verbos a wɔn ni irregular no, ɛsɛ wɔn participio no (go -> gone, see -> seen). Wɔde no: 1) Ma ka ahyɛseɛ a ɛnyɛ adwene biara (e.g., I have visited Paris). 2) Ma ka ahyɛseɛ a ɛda bɛyɛ a na ɛwɔ hɔ ara na ɛyɛ adwene (e.g., I have lost my keys). 3) Wɔde 'already' (ya), 'just' (acaba de), 'yet' (todavía) wɔ mmusuo na nyɛto no mu. 4) Wɔde 'for' na 'since' ma ka ɛda (e.g., I have lived here for 10 years). Wɔ mmusuo no mu, yɛbɔɔ auxiliar no akɔso: Have you finished? Wɔ nyɛto no mu: I have not (haven't) finished. Sonka sɛ wɔde 'yesterday', 'last week' etc., wɔde past simple, na mmom present perfect.

concept_examples.text: I have eaten breakfast.
She has visited Mexico.
We haven't finished our homework yet.
concept_examples.translation: Yɛammra yɛn adwuma no ho adanseɛ.

concept_examples.text: Have you ever seen a shark?

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, yɛka 'lo he visto ayer', nanso wɔ English, present perfect mmom nni adwene a wɔde 'yesterday' ka. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka ahyɛseɛ a ɛyɛ adwene biara, wɔde past simple (saw). Sɛ wode 'have seen' na wunnim adwene no, ɛyɛ adwene ma woka ahyɛseɛ.

levels.label: Forming the Present Perfect
levels.translation: Present Perfect a ɛde bɔɔ so

examples.note: Hwehwɛ sɛ 'have' de bɔɔ 'I've' wɔ English a wɔde ka: I've finished.
Yɛnka 'has' ma third person singular (he, she, it).
Nyɛto no de bɔɔ 'haven't' (have not) anaa 'hasn't' (has not).
Wɔ mmusuo no mu, yɛbɔɔ sujeto no na auxiliar no: Have you...?
Yɛmmere wɔn a yɛkɔe; ahyɛseɛ no nea ɛyɛ adwene.
Participio a ɛyɛ 'eat' no ne 'eaten'.

examples.original: Have you ever seen a ghost?
examples.note: Wɔde 'ever' wɔ mmusuo no mu ma wusua ahyɛseɛ.
Adwene no nea ɛyɛ adwene: nna yɛnnhu.
'Just' de bɔɔ auxiliar no na participio no.

examples.original: I have lived here for five years.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv lɪvd hɪr fɔːr faɪv jɪrz/
examples.note: Yɛnka 'for' ma ɛda (ɛda biara).

title: Imperatives (Affirmative and Negative) / Imperativo (dɔm ne mmara)
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, imperativo no wɔ fa ako a wɔde ma obi a, ɛno ne sɛ obiara a wɔde kasa kyerɛ no. Wɔ Twimu, imperativo no yɛ simple paa: ɛto so ara na ɛyɛ, ɛnyɛ sɛ wɔde kasa kyerɛ obi a. Sɛ 'habla' (tú) ne 'hable' (usted) a, wɔ Twimu ɛne 'speak'. Enti, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woabɔ no ahyɛ a, wɔde 'don't' + verbo, na wɔde 'no' + imperativo wɔ Hispanimu. Nhyira: wɔmmusɛ 'doesn't' ma obiara; 'don't' na wɔde ma obiara.
rule: Wɔ Twimu, imperativo no de verbo no so ara (infinitivo bi 'to'). Wɔde ma obi a, ɛto so ara na ɛyɛ, ɛnyɛ sɛ wɔde kasa kyerɛ obi a. Sɛ 'Open the door', 'Listen to me'. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woabɔ no ahyɛ a, wɔde 'don't' (anaa 'do not' wɔ formal mu) ma verbo no so ara: 'Don't open the door', 'Don't worry'. Ɛnyɛ sɛ wɔde kasa kyerɛ obi a anaa obiara a, na ɛnyɛ sɛ wɔde kasa kyerɛ obi a anaa obiara a. Wɔde 'let's' + verbo ma obi a (e.g., 'Let's go'). Wɔ Twimu, ɛnyɛ sɛ wɔde imperativo ma obi a sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka kyerɛ no sɛ wopɛ sɛ woyɛ (sɛ 'que te mejores'), na wɔde mmara biara ma no.

concept_examples.text: Open the window, please.
Don't touch that!
Let's go to the park.
Please, close the door.

common_error.explanation: Asantefo bɔ sɛ wɔde 'to' maa 'don't' ahyɛ a wɔ Hispanimu (sɛ 'no fumar'). Wɔ Twimu, wɔde verbo no so ara maa 'don't' ahyɛ bi 'to'.

examples.note: Wɔde verbo no so ara bi obiara. Wɔ Hispanimu, 'siéntate' ne obiara a wɔde kasa kyerɛ no.
Imperativo dɔm no yɛ so ara sɛ wɔde kasa kyerɛ obi anaa obiara. Faako sɛ 'listen' ɛnte saa 'to' a ɛma no ahyɛ.

examples.translation: Bra wo nsa a, ma me.
examples.note: Verbo 'come' no so ara na ɛyɛ. Wɔ Hispanimu, 'venir' wɔ hwee mu, nanso wɔ Twimu ɛnyɛ.

examples.translation: Mmra wo ntɛm wɔ akwantu mu.
examples.note: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woabɔ no ahyɛ a, wɔde 'don't' ma verbo no so ara. Wɔ Hispanimu, wɔde 'no' + imperativo.

examples.translation: Mmra wo ho a, wo ntɛm.
examples.note: Ɛwom sɛ 'be' yɛ verbo a ɛyɛ den, nanso wɔ imperativo mmara mu, wɔde 'don't be'.

examples.translation: Mmra wo ho a, wo ho yɛ den.

title: Count and Uncount Nouns / Nnuan ne Nnuan a ɛnyɛ
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, akyirikyiri bi wɔ nnua ne nnua a ɛnyɛ ntɛm, nanso ɛnyɛ pɛn nka. Sɛ waka sɛ 'mmɛbɛ' ma adwene a wɔde ka nnuan a wɔde bɛ ma, na wɔ English mu 'bread' yɛ nnua a ɛnyɛ ntɛm na ɛmmɔ adwene. Akyirikyiribi bi a ɛso: nnuan a ɛnyɛ ntɛm wɔ English mu mmusua 'a/an' anaa 'one', nanso wɔ Twi mu, wɔde 'baako' anaa 'bi' maa nnuan a ɛnyɛ ntɛm sɛ 'baako ahonam' a wɔ English mu woka sɛ 'some information'.
rule: Wɔ English mu, nnuan a wɔde ntɛm ma (count nouns) pɛ sɛ wɔbɛka wɔn wɔ ɛho anaa mmoa mu na wɔde ntɛm ma wɔn (one apple, two apples). Nnuan a ɛnyɛ ntɛm (uncount nouns) nnyɛ mmoa na ɛmmɔ adwene (water, rice, information). Ma wɔde 'some', 'any', 'much', anaa mmea sɛ 'a glass of' anaa 'a piece of' de ntɛm nnuan a ɛnyɛ ntɛm. Ma wɔde 'a/an' de maa ɛho, 'many' de maa mmoa, na 'few' de maa nnuan a wɔwɔ pii. Ma wɔde 'much' na 'little' de maa nnuan a ɛnyɛ ntɛm. Deɛ ɛso wɔ 'the' no, nanso deɛ ɛnyɛ ntɛm no, wɔde 'a/an' mmusua nnuan a ɛnyɛ ntɛm. Nnuan bi wɔ a wɔde ntɛm anaa ɛnyɛ ntɛm ntɛm akyirikyiri (e.g., 'chicken' sɛ ɛyɛ animal anaa sɛ ɛyɛ food).

title: Some and Any / Some ne Any (ne wɔn a wɔ wɔn ho)
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnkyɛ yɛbɛka 'dɛn biara', 'obuo biara' anaa 'dɛn nni' wɔ kyerɛwfoɔ ne afuomfoɔ anaa nhyɛsoɔ no mu. Wɔ Twereko, ahotosoɔ no bi wɔ 'some' ne 'any' a wɔde hyɛ a, ɛno akyi na ɔbɛka a ɛyɛ asɛm bi wɔ kyerɛwfoɔ ne afuomfoɔ anaa nhyɛsoɔ no mu. Nkɔsoɔ pii wɔ hɔ na ɔyɛ a wɔde 'some' bɛka wɔ nhyɛsoɔ no mu ne 'any' wɔ kyerɛwfoɔ no mu, nanso wɔ Twereko no, kyerɛwfoɔ no yɛ ɔyɛ paa. Afei, 'any' wɔ kyerɛwfoɔ no mu kyerɛ 'wɔn a wɔ wɔn ho'.
rule: Yɛbɛka 'some' (ne wɔn a wɔ wɔn ho: somebody, someone, something, somewhere) wɔ kyerɛwfoɔ ne nhyɛsoɔ a yɛde ma fa so anaa yɛde ma fa kɔkɔ bɔ nea yɛpɛ no, anaa yɛde ma fa kɔkɔ bɔ nea yɛpɛ sɛ ɔbɛyɛ. Yɛbɛka 'any' (ne wɔn a wɔ wɔn ho: anybody, anyone, anything, anywhere) wɔ afuomfoɔ ne nhyɛsoɔ a ɛyɛ ɔkwan biara so, sɛnea ɛyɛ wɔ kyerɛwfoɔ a ɛkyerɛ 'wɔn a wɔ wɔn ho' anaa 'ɛnyɛ dɛn'. Wɔn a wɔ wɔn ho no nso siane: something/anything, somebody/anybody, someone/anyone, somewhere/anywhere. Wɔ ɛkɔntomfoɔ no, yɛbɛka 'some' ne ɛkɔntomfoɔ no ne 'any' ne ɛkɔntomfoɔ no; wɔ ɛnnyinafoɔ no, yɛbɛka 'some' anaa 'any' sɛnea ɛyɛ. Yɛmmfa 'no' ne 'any' wɔ asɛm biara mu; yɛbɛka 'no' + ɛkɔntomfoɔ anaa 'not... any'.

title: Much, Many, A lot of / Nkyerɛntɔ
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnka 'pii' anaa 'pii pii' a wɔte nkyerɛkyerɛ ne nkyɛnso no ho, nanso wɔ Twirɛ no, ahotosoɔ no te nkyerɛkyerɛdeɛ no ne nkontomdan no so, ɛnte sɛe ne nkyɛnso no so. Sɛ ɛyɛ adɛn nso a, ɛyɛ anigye: 'many' ma nkontomdan a woka so (e.i. books), 'much' ma nkontomdan a ɛnka so (e.i. water), na 'a lot of' ma mmom ahotosoɔ no nyinaa. Nkɔso a ɛte sɛn ara ne sɛ wɔmo 'much' ne nkontomdan a woka so wɔ nkyerɛkyerɛdeɛ no mu, nanso kyerɛ sɛ 'much' ne 'many' de wɔ mmerɛ ne nyekyerɛ mu.
rule: Wɔ Twirɛ no, 'much', 'many' ne 'a lot of' nkyerɛntɔ a wɔde kyerɛ nkyɛnso. 'Many' de wɔ nkontomdan a woka so ne a wɔwɔ he mmienu (books, cars, friends). 'Much' de wɔ nkontomdan a ɛnka so (water, time, money). Wɔ nkyerɛkyerɛdeɛ no mu, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde 'a lot of' (anaa 'lots of' wɔ nkyerɛkyerɛdeɛ a ɛte sɛn ara mu) ma ahotosoɔ no nyinaa. Wɔ mmerɛ ne nyekyerɛ mu, yɛde 'much' ne 'many'. Yɛde 'how much' nyekyerɛ nkyɛnso a ɛnka so (How much water?), na yɛde 'how many' nyekyerɛ nkyɛnso a woka so (How many books?). Wɔmmusra 'much' anaa 'many' ne nkontomdan a ɛwɔ he kɔkɔ. Wɔde 'too much', 'too many', 'so much', 'so many' ma nkyerɛkyerɛdeɛ a ɛte sɛn ara. Wɔ nkyerɛkyerɛdeɛ no mu, 'much' yɛ nkyerɛkyerɛdeɛ a ɛte sɛn ara anaa ɛte sɛn (There is much work). Ma A2, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde mmerɛ ne nyekyerɛ ne sɛ wɔde 'a lot of' wɔ nkyerɛkyerɛdeɛ no mu. Kyerɛ sɛ wɔmmusra 'much' ne 'many' ne 'no' wɔ nkyerɛkyerɛ a ɛte sɛn ara (de 'not much' anaa 'not many').

title: Relative Clauses: who, which, that / Nsɛmfa a wɔde toto nkurɔfo ne nnuan: who, which, that
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnka 'a' ma nkurɔfo ne nnuan, na ɛnyɛ biribi a yɛde 'obuo' ma nkurɔfo. Wɔ English, ɛsɛ sɛ woode 'who' (ma nkurɔfo) ne 'which' (ma nnuan) ato so, nanso 'that' pɛ sɛ wɔde ma nnuan ne nkurɔfo wɔ mfonini pii. Fa akwantu: wɔ English, ɛnyɛ biribi a wɔde ɛto so sɛ ɛyɛ subject wɔ kyerɛw, nanso wɔ Twi, ɛyɛ biribi a wɔde ɛto so. Enti, wɔ English, wɔnnsusow 'what' ma relative (ɛyɛ ɔkwan a wɔde no wɔ Hispanohablantes); wɔde 'that' anaa 'which' ato so.
rule:
Nsɛmfa a wɔde toto nkurɔfo ne nnuan de ma nkurɔfo ne nnuan a wɔwɔ hɔ. Wɔ English, yɛde:

- **who** ma nkurɔfo (subject anaa object) na, wɔ kasa a ɛnyɛ fɔtrɛ, yɛde no ma nnuan a wɔwɔ din.
- **which** ma nnuan, nnuan anaa adwene.
- **that** de ma nkurɔfo ne nnuan, pɛpɛɛpɛ wɔ nsɛmfa a wɔde toto (restrictive).

Nsɛmfa a ɛne εho te: [noun] + [relative pronoun] + [clause].

Mfatoho:
- The man **who** lives next door is a doctor. (Ono a ɔte wɔ me nni yɛ odi.)
- The book **which** I bought is interesting. (Kitab a mɛto no yɛ pɛnkyerɛ.)
- The dog **that** barks a lot is mine. (Mpae a ɔtɔ so pɛ yɛ me.)

**Nsianka a wɔde wɔ Hispanohablantes:**
- Mmom sɛ wode 'what' ma relative (wɔ Twi 'a' ɛso wɔ mfonini, nanso wɔ English 'what' ne 'a' na wɔde no wɔ biribiara a ɛnni antecedent).
- Mmom sɛ wofi 'who/which/that' so sɛ ɛyɛ subject, efisɛ verb no sɛ subject.
- Bu sɛ wɔ English, ɛsɛ sɛ subject + verb, ɛnyɛ biribi a wɔde ɛto so (mfatoho 'Ono a ɔte wɔ me nni' -> 'The man who lives here', ɛnyɛ 'The man who here lives').

**Nkyea ne nkyerɛkyerɛ:** Ɛnyɛ biribi a wɔde ɛto so. 'That' pɛ sɛ wɔde ma nkurɔfo ne nnuan. 'Who' ma nkurɔfo. 'Which' ma nnuan. Wɔ English a wɔkasa no wɔ ɛno, 'that' yɛ pɛnkyerɛ wɔ kasa a ɛnyɛ fɔtrɛ, nanso 'who' ne 'which' yɛ fɔtrɛ.

examples.note: Yɛde 'which' efisɛ yɛka nnuan (efie).

examples.original: The movie which we watched was boring.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈmuːvi wɪtʃ wiː wɒtʃt wɒz ˈbɔːrɪŋ/
examples.note: Wɔ hɛn, 'which' yɛ object, nanso yɛde no, ɛnyɛ biribi a yɛfi no so.

examples.original: The cat that is on the table is black.
examples.phonetic: /ðə kæt ðæt ɪz ɒn ðə ˈteɪbəl ɪz blæk/
examples.translation: Mpae a ɔte wɔ table no yɛ black.
examples.note: 'That' pɛ sɛ wɔde ma nnuan ne nkurɔfo.

examples.original: The boy that you met is my cousin.
examples.phonetic: /ðə bɔɪ ðæt juː mɛt ɪz maɪ ˈkʌzən/
examples.translation: Mma a woka no yɛ me mmarima.
examples.note: 'That' pɛ sɛ wɔde ma nkurɔfo a ɛnni 'who', pɛpɛɛpɛ wɔ English a wɔkasa no.

translations.tw: Nsɛmfa a wɔde toto nkurɔfo ne nnuan (who, which, that)
